Findings, fixes and remaining validation

Targeted real Clerk authentication — 2026-10-01

Real Clerk, the running production frontend/API and configured application PostgreSQL were used. Session restoration, natural JWT expiry/renewal, sign-out boundaries and same-account reauthentication passed. Full session expiry, explicit backend revocation, reciprocal ownership isolation and dedicated-account deletion are blocked, not simulated passes.

The observed JWT lifetime was 60 seconds. After a 63,331 ms natural wait, the retained expired JWT received HTTP 401; a genuine newly minted JWT received HTTP 200 with later issuance/expiry timestamps and the same Clerk session. Dashboard reload, protected Settings and a fresh browser context using copied saved state passed. No clocks, tokens, ownership responses or database access were mocked or modified. Clerk distinguishes its short JWT lifetime from its longer session lifetime in its session model. Full session expiration/inactivity expiration was not exercised: those configured deadlines were days away. UI sign-out subsequently changed the original session to removed, and human sign-in created a different session for the same user. Protected project API access and reload passed after recovery. This is sign-out and reauthentication evidence, not explicit sessions.revokeSession coverage.

Signup in bundled Chromium encountered an operator-reported Cloudflare CAPTCHA refresh loop. Installed Chrome was tried with normal CAPTCHA protections intact; the operator chose sign-in instead. The safety guard proved that the signed-in identity predated this run and rejected it as a disposable fixture. No disposable A/B account, project, document or telemetry record was created. The four dedicated-account-dependent Playwright cases were explicitly skipped for missing fixtures. Read/list/edit/export/rename/delete isolation in both directions and unchanged records after denied mutations therefore remain unverified. Cloudflare documents that automated browsers can be unsupported by its challenges; this is a possible explanation, not a proven cause of this specific loop. Cloudflare browser support.

Deletion source review confirmed that account.deleteData deletes the local users row and relies on foreign-key cascades for projects, documents, keys, sessions and messages. The actual Privacy UI requires DELETE, calls that endpoint, then opens Clerk account management to complete identity deletion. The endpoint does not delete the Clerk identity or revoke its sessions. Authenticated requests can auto-provision a fresh empty local user while the identity remains active. These are implementation findings, not live deletion or cascade evidence. No deletion endpoint or UI was exercised because no account was created specifically for deletion; the existing account was preserved.

All preexisting database rows retained their IDs and whole-row hashes in all six tables: 1 user, 35 projects, 66 documents, 1 provider key, 36 sessions and 163 messages. The completed project c75d5a6b-fdb8-4ffe-89dc-1209e1864221 remains intact. No accounts or application records were deleted. Existing artifacts and reports were copied into the new archive before writes. The original e2e/storage-state/user.json is unchanged; it refers to the now removed original session. Usable refreshed authentication is retained separately as saved-reauthenticated.json in this run's archive. Original and refreshed state, raw traces and videos are sensitive local artifacts and are not embedded in HTML.

No confirmed product defect was found and no product implementation changed. The first restoration attempt requested a token before Clerk had loaded after navigation; adding a readiness wait fixed that harness failure and the focused rerun passed. The saved sign-out runner passed all recorded boundary assertions but timed out during the human recovery pause after a long elapsed interval. The first recovery attempt required a sign-in form even though human sign-in had already restored access; accepting the authenticated state corrected that selector expectation. The final standalone recovery rerun passed and established the changed session, same identity, HTTP 200 and reload. These retained failures are harness/interaction/environment outcomes, not product failures. Automatic triage is heuristic; the classifications in this report use the actual evidence.

Runner executions are retained separately: 1 passed saved-session rerun; 1 passed final recovery rerun; 4 skipped disposable-dependent cases. The saved sign-out runner failed at the HITL timeout despite its persisted passing boundary assertions; the earlier renewal and recovery failures and interrupted signup attempts are preserved. This is not a single all-passing live suite. Web typecheck, frontend lint, helper syntax and git diff --check passed. The standalone HTML opened at desktop/mobile sizes, verified all 14 auth rows (8 passed / 6 blocked), renewal/recovery/database evidence and source search, with no page errors or mobile overflow. QA screenshots and final check logs are retained in the archive. Since there was no product change, no fresh build, unit/integration run or full deterministic browser rerun was needed. Earlier 141 deterministic passes / 1 skip, 73 unit passes, 25 disposable PostgreSQL integration passes and zero audit findings remain prior results, not expanded real-auth coverage.

Final listeners and process commands confirm the usable production real-auth frontend on 3000, PID 10776, and API on 4000, PID 8036. No server was replaced or stopped, and .next was not rebuilt while browser tests ran. Final readiness returned 200; unauthenticated project/AI boundaries returned 401; protected frontend requests returned 404 with and without the spoofed test header. Authenticated project requests returned 200 in the final recovery test. PLAYWRIGHT=0 and ENABLE_AI_TRIAGE=false were retained.

Zero paid provider requests, zero provider-key verification requests, and zero AI triage requests. Unauthenticated AI boundary probes returned 401 before any provider call. Spending guards blocked no attempted paid operation. No commit or deployment occurred. The truncating integration suite was not run, database guards were unchanged, and application DATABASE_URL was not replaced.

Artifact archive: .freebuff/auth-testing/20261001-200010/. It contains copied historical artifacts/reports, original and separate refreshed state, timestamped runner directories, screenshots, traces, videos, sanitized API-status JSONL, Clerk lifetime/renewal/sign-out/recovery evidence, database baseline/final hashes, server boundary/process evidence and final-verification-summary.json. test-results/auth-runs.json points to this summary; regenerated HTML keeps all historical results separate and includes the actual auth scenario/attempt ledger.

The remaining work requires two disposable accounts created for testing, including one specifically for deletion, plus a practical way to exercise real session expiration. Backend revocation must use supported Clerk mechanisms; no revocation, expiration, ownership or deletion result should be inferred from deterministic coverage or source review.

Testing and fixes — consolidated deterministic execution 2026-10-01

PostgreSQL integration and production audit refresh — 2026-10-01

25 integration tests passed across 5 files in 113.67 seconds, with zero failures. This is a fresh execution on real, disposable Supabase PostgreSQL through the Session pooler, not the configured application database. Read-only preflight verified current_database() = devdocs_e2e_test, an empty public schema before migrations, and a different application host/database name. The existing _test name guard stayed enabled. The suite applied committed migrations, created test rows and truncated only this verified test target. Post-run read-only checks found the six expected application tables and zero rows in all six. The test schema is retained for future integration runs.

Integration filePassedWhat was exercised
projects.test.ts11Project lifecycle, ownership and validation
documents.test.ts2Document backfill, editing and ownership
sessions.test.ts2Interview-session persistence and ownership
account.test.ts2Owned-data export and account cascade deletion
keys.test.ts8Encryption, masking, rotation and preservation on provider errors

The database is real; provider verification responses in key tests remain doubles. These results do not expand real Clerk, paid provider or browser coverage. ENABLE_AI_TRIAGE=false; no paid requests or provider-key verification occurred. Application DATABASE_URL, existing live projects, browser storage and earlier artifacts were preserved. Only the test URL's host/path were corrected during setup, with private environment backups kept in the ignored archive and no secrets displayed.

The direct endpoint was unreachable on this machine's IPv4 connection. After the user selected the Session pooler, its URL still selected postgres; the guard rejected it before SQL. The path was corrected to devdocs_e2e_test. An initial pnpm command rejected --outputFile before starting tests; the corrected command used run test. A cleanup helper initially misquoted a qualified table identifier (PostgreSQL 42P01); correcting that helper made the read-only check pass. These were configuration/harness issues, not product defects. Hook/test timeouts were bounded at 120/30 seconds for remote latency; test assertions, retry behavior and the database guard were unchanged.

The fresh production audit found one low DOMPurify advisory in posthog-js@1.404.1 > dompurify@3.4.13, with zero moderate/high/critical findings. The root override now selects DOMPurify 3.4.16, the patched version for GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p. Only that override and its lockfile dependency references/integrity changed; other dependency versions and existing uncommitted changes were preserved. The post-fix pnpm audit --prod --json exited 0 with zero findings across 442 production dependencies. The advisory's special in-place sanitation hook conditions were not reproduced in this app; this is a dependency fix, not evidence of a confirmed application exploit.

Compatibility checks passed: forced typecheck (3 tasks), forced lint (1 task), fresh real-auth web production build, isolated API/web production smoke and portable HTML report verification on desktop/mobile. Confirmed results

  • Browser suite: 125 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures, 0 flaky tests in one 126-case run (21.7 minutes). The skip is the desktop instance of a mobile-only sheet test. No unexpected console errors were found across the artifacts.
  • Isolated API/provider/browser-stream suite: 62 passed, including the long-history regression added after the full browser run.
  • PostgreSQL integration suite: 25 passed using a newly initialized local PostgreSQL 15.18 cluster, committed migrations, and a database named devdocs_e2e_test. Provider verification was mocked; database writes and encryption were real. The temporary server was stopped afterward.
  • Compiled API smoke: passed.
  • Production dependency audit: 0 findings across the 441 dependencies reported by pnpm audit --prod.
  • Typecheck: all three packages passed. Frontend lint: passed.
  • Agent failure digest: no failed tests. git diff --check: passed.
  • Web production build: passed. Production authentication smoke: passed: homepage/security headers, unauthenticated protected routes, spoofed test and middleware headers, and absence of mock identity in shipped browser chunks.

Earlier browser runs found test-selector ambiguity after the Next upgrade and when a mobile document dialog covered the chat download button. The selectors were corrected. They also exposed a real homepage overflow defect, which was fixed with responsive navigation and content grids.

The production smoke initially failed because the harness mixed 127.0.0.1 and localhost, causing Clerk's internal rewrite to become a proxy request. Using the same listening and request hostname resolved the harness failure.

Product defects fixed

  • AI chat openers and clarification replies could overwrite saved documents. Only explicit generation requests now persist documents, and completion waits for persistence.
  • Empty or truncated provider replies could be marked complete. They now produce recoverable errors. Cancellation clears the stream timeout and stops the provider request.
  • Retrying a failed generation lost its completion action. Retry now preserves the original action and avoids duplicating the user's chat message.
  • Skipped domains were local-only. Deferred documentation now saves before progress advances, with a retry path on failure.
  • Editing merged Markdown by splitting horizontal rules could mix domain content. Editing now saves each domain explicitly, retains failed drafts, and disables export while changes are unsaved.
  • Failed project hydration could leave an indefinite skeleton. Load errors now display a retry action; malformed saved interview fields are validated.
  • Several mutations lacked visible failure handling. Project/template errors now show feedback, and retrying template initialization reuses its project.
  • Mobile layouts, action-menu positioning, hidden sheet focus, key-input masking, document/settings deep links, and search edge cases were corrected.
  • A request header could enable the web authentication bypass. Mock identity now requires an explicit development test server; production uses Clerk.
  • The compiled API could not start because of unresolved module imports. It now builds a runnable Node bundle, checked by a startup smoke test.
  • The rate-limit counter and expiry were separate operations. A single Redis script now updates both and repairs keys with no expiry.
  • Vulnerable production dependencies were updated, including Next 15.5.24, React 19 compatibility, Hono, Drizzle, and affected transitive packages.
  • Long generated replies could exceed the API's 4,000-character history limit on the next request. Only the recent context sent to the provider is now bounded; stored messages and exported documents remain intact.

The Next upgrade addresses published advisories, including the Windows server advisory.

        {
          "version": "3.4.13",
          "paths": [
            "apps\\web > posthog-js@1.404.1 > dompurify@3.4.13"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "found_by": null,
      "deleted": null,
      "references": "- https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p\n- https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/pull/1636\n- https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/commit/b9b9d80f7e401771c2ccaef5f45def7eec8f27d7\n- https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/releases/tag/3.4.16\n- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p",
      "created": "2026-09-30T15:37:57.000Z",
      "id": 1240621,
      "npm_advisory_id": null,
      "overview": "## Summary\n\nIn `IN_PLACE` mode DOMPurify sanitizes the caller's live DOM subtree directly. To close a known hazard (GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7), the library neutralizes any node a hook detaches during sanitization by stripping its subtree's non-allow-listed attributes, but this neutralization is wired only into the `beforeSanitizeElements` and `uponSanitizeElement` hook sites. An `afterSanitizeElements` or `afterSanitizeAttributes` hook that removes a non-root element (a documented, supported pattern) detaches that element's subtree with no neutralization, so descendant `on*` handlers remain armed on the caller's live tree after `sanitize()` returns, yielding DOM XSS. No special privilege is required beyond supplying markup to an application that uses `IN_PLACE` together with a node-removing afterSanitize hook.\n\n## Root Cause\n\n`IN_PLACE` sanitization mutates the caller's live document, so any element a hook detaches from that tree must have its subtree neutralized before `sanitize()` returns; otherwise a queued resource-event handler (for example an `<img onerror>` that began loading when the caller built the tree) fires in page scope even though the handler never reached the sanitized output. The guard helper `_handleHookDetachedNode` (which calls `_neutralizeSubtree` in `IN_PLACE`) is invoked only after `beforeSanitizeElements` and after `uponSanitizeElement`. It is never invoked from the afterSanitize return paths, and `_sanitizeAttributes` never calls it at all. The post-walk `IN_PLACE` neutralization pass iterates only `DOMPurify.removed`, and hook-detached nodes are intentionally not recorded there, so that pass cannot reach them either.\n\n```text\nsrc/purify.ts\n  _sanitizeElements: _handleHookDetachedNode present at lines 2142 and 2175\n    (before/upon), absent after afterSanitizeElements at lines 2208 and 2249.\n  _sanitizeAttributes: afterSanitizeAttributes fires at line 2670 with no\n    detach re-check; the function never calls _handleHookDetachedNode.\n  Post-walk IN_PLACE pass (lines 3081-3090) iterates DOMPurify.removed only,\n    which by design (comment at lines 2096-2099) excludes hook-detached nodes.\n```\n\n## Impact\n\nAn attacker who supplies markup processed by a victim application that runs `DOMPurify.sanitize(node, { IN_PLACE: true })` and registers a node-removing `afterSanitizeElements` or `afterSanitizeAttributes` hook can retain arbitrary `on*` event handlers on descendants of a removed non-root element. Because `IN_PLACE` operates on the caller's live document, a queued resource-event handler on such a descendant fires in the page origin after the synchronous `sanitize()` call returns, giving script execution in the victim's session (DOM XSS). This defeats DOMPurify's `IN_PLACE` contract to neutralize handlers on subtrees removed from the live tree. The capability is script execution in the victim origin; exact confidentiality and integrity effects depend on the hosting application's session.\n\n## Proof of Concept\n\n```text\nDependencies: Node.js and jsdom. The harness builds a live tree, registers a\nremoval hook, runs IN_PLACE sanitize(), then inspects whether the attacker\nonerror handler survives on the detached descendant. jsdom does not perform\nreal image loads, so the retained handler (rather than an actual fired event)\nis the observed hazard; the retained on* attribute on a live detached node\nafter a synchronous sanitize() return is the neutralization failure.\n```\n\nReproduction steps:\n1. Build a live subtree `#root > section#wrap > img[onerror]` where `#root` is the walk root and `section#wrap` is a non-root wrapper.\n2. Register an `afterSanitizeElements` (or `afterSanitizeAttributes`) hook that calls `node.remove()` on the wrapper.\n3. Call `DOMPurify.sanitize(root, { IN_PLACE: true })`.\n4. Observe that the descendant `<img>` retains its `onerror` handler, whereas the same removal performed in a `beforeSanitizeElements`/`uponSanitizeElement` hook strips it.\n\n```javascript\nconst { JSDOM } = require('jsdom');\nconst createDOMPurify = require('dompurify');\nconst { window } = new JSDOM('<!DOCTYPE html><body></body>');\nconst DOMPurify = createDOMPurify(window);\n\nconst root = window.document.createElement('div');\nroot.id = 'root';\nroot.innerHTML = '<section id=\"wrap\"><img src=\"x\" onerror=\"ATTACKER()\"></section>';\nwindow.document.body.appendChild(root);\n\nDOMPurify.addHook('afterSanitizeElements', (node) => {\n  if (node.id === 'wrap') node.remove();\n});\nDOMPurify.sanitize(root, { IN_PLACE: true });\n\n// The detached <img> still carries its onerror handler:\nconsole.log(root.querySelector('#wrap') === null,               // true (removed from live tree)\n            !!window.document.querySelector('img[onerror]') ||  // handler survives on the detached node\n            root.innerHTML);\n```\n\n```text\nPASS: beforeSanitizeElements detach neutralizes descendant onerror (control)\nPASS: uponSanitizeElement detach neutralizes descendant onerror (control)\nPASS: without a removal hook the descendant onerror is stripped normally\nPASS: afterSanitizeElements detach LEAVES descendant onerror armed (GAP)\nPASS: afterSanitizeAttributes detach LEAVES descendant onerror armed (GAP)\nPASS: kept custom element removed in afterSanitizeElements leaves descendant onerror armed (GAP)\n```\n\n## Attack Chain\n\n1. **Exposure:** The victim application calls `DOMPurify.sanitize(liveNode, { IN_PLACE: true })` on attacker-influenced markup and has registered a node-removing `afterSanitizeElements` or `afterSanitizeAttributes` hook per an application policy (`src/purify.ts:3026` walk, `2136` element pass, `2522` attribute pass).\n2. **Control:** The attacker controls the markup, including a non-root wrapper element and, inside it, a descendant carrying an `on*` resource-event handler such as `<img src=x onerror=...>`.\n3. **Path:** The pre-order walk visits the wrapper before its descendants. During the wrapper's element or attribute pass the application hook detaches the wrapper from the live tree.\n4. **Guard:** The detach-neutralization guard `_handleHookDetachedNode` runs only after `beforeSanitizeElements` (`2142`) and `uponSanitizeElement` (`2175`); it is absent after `afterSanitizeElements` (`2208`, `2249`) and is never called by `_sanitizeAttributes` (afterSanitizeAttributes at `2670`). The NodeIterator advances past the detached subtree, so the descendants are never revisited, and the post-walk pass iterates only `DOMPurify.removed`, which excludes hook-detached nodes.\n5. **Primitive:** The descendant retains its `on*` handler on the caller's live document after `sanitize()` returns.\n6. **Result:** The queued resource event fires the attacker handler in the victim page origin, achieving DOM XSS despite `IN_PLACE` sanitization.\n\n## Bypass Evidence\n\nThe relevant prior fix is GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 (\"IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable, causing XSS\"), whose change (`#1557`) added `_neutralizeSubtree` at the `beforeSanitizeElements` and `uponSanitizeElement` detach sites. Inspection of that change shows it touches no afterSanitize site: the diff adds the neutralization only at the before/upon locations, later refactored into `_handleHookDetachedNode` at `src/purify.ts:2142` and `2175`. A subsequent hardening change (`#1616`) added a `rootWasRemoved` throw and a neutralization sweep over `DOMPurify.removed`, but that sweep still iterates only `DOMPurify.removed`, which by design excludes hook-detached non-root nodes, so it does not close this gap. The `afterSanitizeElements`-on-kept-custom-element site at `2208` was itself introduced by the fix for GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4 (`#1527`), adding another uncovered hook site.\n\nDisproof attempts, all failed: (a) that a later release closed the afterSanitize gap, refuted by inspecting the published 3.4.13, 3.4.14, and 3.4.15 artifacts; (b) that detached descendants are revisited or re-sanitized, refuted at runtime (the `onerror` is retained only at the afterSanitize sites and stripped at the before/upon sites and with no removal hook); (c) that the post-walk pass catches hook-detached nodes, refuted by the design that excludes them from `DOMPurify.removed`; (d) that the precondition is contrived, refuted by parity with the accepted GHSA-55q2 threat model and the library's own supported pattern of removing a node inside `afterSanitizeElements`. The only edge not directly executed is the browser resource-event dispatch (jsdom performs no real image load); it is established by the proven retention of the live handler after a synchronous return, the library's own comments describing exactly this hazard, and parity with the accepted GHSA-55q2 mechanism.\n\n## Affected Versions\n\n- `Ecosystem: npm`\n- `Package: dompurify`\n- `Confirmed affected range: >= 3.4.13, <= 3.4.15`\n- `Latest release checked: 3.4.15 (npm registry)`\n- `Fix status: fixed in 3.4.16`\n\nThe before/upon detach neutralization introduced for GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 first shipped in 3.4.13; the residual afterSanitize gap was verified by reproducing it against the published npm artifacts for 3.4.13, 3.4.14, and 3.4.15. The 3.4.12 artifact predates that neutralization and behaves differently at the before/upon sites, so it is outside this specific incomplete-fix range. No release through 3.4.15 neutralizes detached subtrees at the afterSanitize sites, so no fixed version is established.\n\n## Suggested Fix\n\nEnforce the same `IN_PLACE` detach-neutralization invariant at every hook site that can detach a node, not only the before/upon sites. Concretely, apply a `_handleHookDetachedNode(currentNode, root)` re-check after `afterSanitizeElements` at both `src/purify.ts:2208` and `2249` (returning as removed when the node was detached), and add an equivalent `IN_PLACE` detach check plus `_neutralizeSubtree` after `afterSanitizeAttributes` at `2670`. As an interim mitigation without a code change, applications using `IN_PLACE` can avoid removing nodes inside `afterSanitizeElements`/`afterSanitizeAttributes` hooks and instead perform such removals in `beforeSanitizeElements`/`uponSanitizeElement`, or avoid `IN_PLACE` for attacker-influenced content.\n\nReported by zx (GitHub: @manus-pi).",

+// Live auth evidence only. No integration setup, provider calls, or SQL writes.
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { parse } from 'dotenv';
+import postgres from 'postgres';
+const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));
+const run = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, '.freebuff/auth-testing/current-run.txt'), 'utf8').trim();
+const env = parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'apps/api/.env')));
+const web = parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'apps/web/.env.local')));
+Object.assign(process.env, { CLERK_SECRET_KEY: env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY });
+const { clerkClient } = await import('@clerk/express');
+const sql = postgres(env.DATABASE_URL, { max: 1, prepare: false, connect_timeout: 15 });
+const tables = ['users', 'projects', 'documentation_bundles', 'user_api_keys', 'interview_sessions', 'interview_messages'];
+async function snapshot() {
+  const result = {};
+  for (const table of tables) result[table] = await sql`select id, md5(row_to_json(t)::text) hash from ${sql(table)} t order by id`;
+  return result;
+}
+try {
+  const [mode, value] = process.argv.slice(2);
+  if (mode === 'baseline') {
+    const records = await snapshot();
+    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(run, 'database-baseline.json'), JSON.stringify(records, null, 2));
+    const config = { webClerkConfigured: !!web.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, apiClerkConfigured: !!env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY,
+      clerkSecretsMatch: !!env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY && env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY === web.CLERK_SECRET_KEY,
+      applicationDatabaseConfigured: !!env.DATABASE_URL, webUrlMatches: env.WEB_URL === 'http://localhost:3000',
+      capturedAt: new Date().toISOString(), counts: Object.fromEntries(tables.map(t => [t, records[t].length])) };
+    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(run, 'configuration.json'), JSON.stringify(config, null, 2));
+    console.log(JSON.stringify(config));
+  } else if (mode === 'identity') {
+    const user = await clerkClient.users.getUser(value);
+    const local = await sql`select id from users where clerk_id = ${value}`;
+    console.log(JSON.stringify({ clerkId: user.id, createdAt: user.createdAt, localId: local[0]?.id ?? null }));
+  } else if (mode === 'revoke') {
+    const session = await clerkClient.sessions.getSession(value);
+    const user = await clerkClient.users.getUser(session.userId);
+    const record = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(run, 'accounts.json')));
+    if (!Object.values(record).some(a => a.clerkId === user.id && a.createdAt >= Date.parse(record.startedAt))) throw new Error('Dedicated run account required');
+    const revoked = await clerkClient.sessions.revokeSession(value);
+    console.log(JSON.stringify({ status: revoked.status, revokedAt: new Date().toISOString(), mechanism: 'Clerk Backend API sessions.revokeSession' }));
+  } else if (mode === 'session' || mode === 'saved-session') {
+    let sessionId = value;
+    if (mode === 'saved-session') {
+      const state = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(run, 'saved-original-copy.json')));
+      const jwt = state.cookies.find(cookie => cookie.name === '__session')?.value;
+      sessionId = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(jwt.split('.')[1], 'base64url').toString()).sid;
+    }
+    const session = await clerkClient.sessions.getSession(sessionId);
+    console.log(JSON.stringify({ status: session.status, expireAt: session.expireAt, abandonAt: session.abandonAt }));
+  } else if (mode === 'snapshot') {
+    const current = await snapshot();
+    const before = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(run, 'database-baseline.json')));
+    const unchanged = Object.fromEntries(tables.map(t => [t, before[t].every(row => current[t].some(r => r.id === row.id && r.hash === row.hash))]));
+    const record = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(run, 'accounts.json')));
+    const owned = {};
+    for (const label of ['A', 'B']) {
+      const account = record[label];
+      if (!account) continue;
+      const user = await sql`select id from users where clerk_id = ${account.clerkId}`;
+      const project = await sql`select id, user_id, name, status, deleted_at, md5(row_to_json(p)::text) hash from projects p where user_id = ${account.localId}`;
+      const documents = await sql`select d.id, d.project_id, d.domain_id, md5(row_to_json(d)::text) hash from documentation_bundles d join projects p on p.id = d.project_id where p.user_id = ${account.localId}`;
+      const sessions = await sql`select id from interview_sessions where user_id = ${account.localId}`;
+      const messages = await sql`select m.id from interview_messages m join interview_sessions s on s.id = m.session_id where s.user_id = ${account.localId}`;
+      const keys = await sql`select id from user_api_keys where user_id = ${account.localId}`;
+      owned[label] = { user, projects: project, documents, sessions, messages, keys };
+    }
+    const result = { at: new Date().toISOString(), preexistingUnchanged: unchanged, owned, counts: Object.fromEntries(tables.map(t => [t, current[t].length])) };
+    if (value) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(run, value + '.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
+    console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
+  } else throw new Error('Unknown evidence operation');
+} catch (error) {
+  console.error(JSON.stringify({ errorType: error.name, errorCode: error.code ?? error.status ?? null }));
+  process.exitCode = 1;
+} finally { await sql.end({ timeout: 5 }); }

+// Read-only checks for the configured live lane. Never prints credential values.
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import { parse } from 'dotenv';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import postgres from 'postgres';
+const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));
+const api = parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'apps/api/.env')));
+const web = parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'apps/web/.env.local')));
+const liveFile = path.join(root, 'apps/web/e2e/.env');
+const live = fs.existsSync(liveFile) ? parse(fs.readFileSync(liveFile)) : {};
+const present = value => Boolean(value && !/your[_-]|placeholder/i.test(value));
+const summary = {
+  credentials: {
+    database: present(api.DATABASE_URL),
+    apiClerkSecret: present(api.CLERK_SECRET_KEY),
+    apiClerkPublishable: present(api.CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY),
+    webClerkSecret: present(web.CLERK_SECRET_KEY),
+    webClerkPublishable: present(web.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY),
+    publishableKeysMatch: api.CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ? api.CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY === web.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY : null,
+    secretKeysMatch: api.CLERK_SECRET_KEY === web.CLERK_SECRET_KEY,
+    encryptionKeyValid: /^[a-f\d]{64}$/i.test(api.ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? ''),
+    aiTriageEnabled: live.ENABLE_AI_TRIAGE === 'true' || process.env.ENABLE_AI_TRIAGE === 'true',
+  },
+  routing: {
+    webUsesLocalApi: web.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL === 'http://localhost:4000',
+    apiAcceptsLocalWeb: api.WEB_URL === 'http://localhost:3000',
+    liveUsesLocalWeb: !live.BASE_URL || live.BASE_URL === 'http://localhost:3000',
+  },
+};
+try {
+  const pk = web.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? '';
+  const host = Buffer.from(pk.replace(/^pk_(test|live)_/, ''), 'base64').toString().replace(/\$$/, '');
+  if (!/^[a-z\d.-]+$/i.test(host)) throw new Error('invalid publishable key');
+  const responses = await Promise.all([
+    fetch('https://api.clerk.com/v1/jwks', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${api.CLERK_SECRET_KEY}` }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) }),
+    fetch(`https://${host}/.well-known/jwks.json`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) }),
+  ]);
+  summary.clerk = { secretAccepted: responses[0].ok, frontendReachable: responses[1].ok };
+  if (responses.every(r => r.ok)) {
+    const [backend, frontend] = await Promise.all(responses.map(r => r.json()));
+    summary.clerk.instanceMatches = backend.keys?.some(a => frontend.keys?.some(b => a.kid === b.kid && a.n === b.n && a.e === b.e)) ?? false;
+  }
+} catch (error) {
+  summary.clerk = { checkFailed: true, errorType: error.name, errorCode: error.cause?.code };
+}
+const sql = postgres(api.DATABASE_URL, { max: 1, prepare: false, connect_timeout: 15 });
+try {
+  await sql`select 1`;
+  const columns = await sql`select table_name, column_name, data_type from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name in ('users','projects','documentation_bundles','user_api_keys','interview_sessions','interview_messages') order by table_name, ordinal_position`;
+  const counts = await sql`select (select count(*)::int from users) users, (select count(*)::int from users where clerk_id is not null) linked_users, (select count(*)::int from projects) projects, (select count(*)::int from documentation_bundles) documents, (select count(*)::int from user_api_keys) provider_keys, (select count(*)::int from interview_sessions) sessions, (select count(*)::int from interview_messages) messages`;
+  summary.database = { connected: true, columns, counts: counts[0] };
+  const migrationTable = await sql`select to_regclass('drizzle.__drizzle_migrations')::text name`;
+  summary.database.migrations = migrationTable[0].name
+    ? await sql`select id, created_at from drizzle.__drizzle_migrations order by id`
+    : [];
+  const stateFile = path.join(root, 'apps/web/e2e/storage-state/user.json');
+  if (fs.existsSync(stateFile)) {
+    const state = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(stateFile, 'utf8'));
+    const sessionCookie = state.cookies?.find(c => c.name === '__session' && c.value);
+    if (sessionCookie) {
+      // Only resolve the identity already authenticated by the browser/API.
+      // Decoding this claim is diagnostic; it is not token verification.
+      const claims = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(sessionCookie.value.split('.')[1], 'base64url').toString());
+      const identity = await sql`select id from users where clerk_id = ${claims.sub}`;
+      if (identity.length) {
+        const projects = await sql`select count(*)::int count from projects where user_id = ${identity[0].id} and deleted_at is null`;
+        const keys = await sql`select provider from user_api_keys where user_id = ${identity[0].id}`;
+        summary.database.browserIdentity = { mapped: true, activeProjects: projects[0].count, configuredProviders: keys.map(k => k.provider) };
+      } else summary.database.browserIdentity = { mapped: false };
+    }
+  }
+  let projectId = process.argv[3];
+  if (projectId === 'latest-live') {
+    const latest = await sql`select id from projects where name like 'E2E Interview %' order by created_at desc limit 1`;
+    projectId = latest[0]?.id;
+  }
+  const reportFile = path.join(root, 'apps/web/test-results/results.json');
+  if (!projectId && fs.existsSync(reportFile)) {
+    const findProject = suites => {
+      for (const suite of suites ?? []) {
+        for (const spec of suite.specs ?? []) for (const test of spec.tests ?? []) {
+          for (const result of test.results ?? []) for (const attachment of result.attachments ?? []) {
+            if (attachment.name !== 'live-project') continue;
+            const body = attachment.path ? fs.readFileSync(attachment.path, 'utf8') : Buffer.from(attachment.body, 'base64').toString();
+            return JSON.parse(body).projectId;
+          }
+        }
+        const nested = findProject(suite.suites);
+        if (nested) return nested;
+      }
+    };
+    projectId = findProject(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(reportFile)).suites);
+  }
+  if (projectId && /^[a-f\d-]{36}$/i.test(projectId)) {
+    const project = await sql`select id, type, status, interview_data->'completedDomains' completed_domains, interview_data->>'currentDomain' current_domain from projects where id = ${projectId}`;
+    const documents = await sql`select domain_id, length(content)::int content_chars from documentation_bundles where project_id = ${projectId} order by domain_id`;
+    const sessions = await sql`select total_messages, total_domains_completed, is_complete, primary_provider from interview_sessions where project_id = ${projectId}`;
+    const messages = await sql`select m.role, m.domain_id, m.provider, m.error_type, count(*)::int count from interview_messages m join interview_sessions s on m.session_id = s.id where s.project_id = ${projectId} group by m.role, m.domain_id, m.provider, m.error_type order by m.domain_id, m.role`;
+    summary.database.liveProject = { project: project[0] ?? null, documents, sessions, messages };
+  }
+} catch (error) {
+  summary.database = { connected: false, errorType: error.name, errorCode: error.code };
+  process.exitCode = 1;
+} finally { await sql.end({ timeout: 5 }); }
+const { columns, ...database } = summary.database ?? {};
+console.log(JSON.stringify({ ...summary, database: { ...database, columnCount: columns?.length } }, null, 2));
+if (process.argv[2]) fs.writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2));

+import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';

+// Intentionally isolated credentials: this check must never use a real database.

+  env: { ...process.env, PORT: '0', NODE_ENV: 'production', DATABASE_URL: 'postgresql://test:test@127.0.0.1:9/devdocs_test', WEB_URL: 'http://localhost:3000', SENTRY_DSN: '', UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL: '', UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN: '' },

+      const match = output.match(/running at http:\/\/localhost:(\d+)/);

+    });
+    child.stderr.on('data', chunk => { output += chunk.toString(); });
+    child.once('exit', code => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(new Error(`API exited with ${code}: ${output}`)); });

+  });

+  assert.match(await (await fetch(base + '/metrics')).text(), /devdocs/);

+} finally { child.kill(); }

+++ b/apps/api/scripts/verify-test-database.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+// Read-only test target verification. Never prints connection strings or passwords.
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { parse } from 'dotenv';
+import postgres from 'postgres';
+
+const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));
+const output = process.argv[2];
+let sql;
+let result;
+let configurationEvidence = {};
+try {
+  const env = parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'apps/api/.env')));
+  const testUrl = new URL(env.TEST_DATABASE_URL ?? '');
+  const appUrl = new URL(env.DATABASE_URL ?? '');
+  const databaseName = testUrl.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).at(-1) ?? '';
+  const appDatabaseName = appUrl.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).at(-1) ?? '';
+  configurationEvidence = { testUrlPresent: true, configuredDatabase: databaseName,
+    nameGuardSatisfied: databaseName.toLowerCase().includes('_test'),
+    applicationHostDifferent: testUrl.hostname !== appUrl.hostname,
+    applicationDatabaseNameDifferent: databaseName !== appDatabaseName,
+    supabaseDirectEndpoint: /^db\.[a-z0-9]+\.supabase\.co$/i.test(testUrl.hostname),
+    hostPlaceholderDetected: /YOUR_TEST_HOST|YOUR_HOST|PROJECT.?REF|[<>]/i.test(testUrl.hostname),
+    passwordPlaceholderDetected: /YOUR.?PASSWORD|YOUR_PASSWORD|<password>/i.test(decodeURIComponent(testUrl.password)) };
+  if (!['postgres:', 'postgresql:'].includes(testUrl.protocol)) throw new Error('InvalidProtocol');
+  if (!databaseName.toLowerCase().includes('_test')) throw new Error('GuardRejectedDatabaseName');
+  if (testUrl.hostname === appUrl.hostname && databaseName === appDatabaseName) throw new Error('ApplicationDatabaseTargetRejected');
+  if (process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL && process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL !== env.TEST_DATABASE_URL) throw new Error('ConflictingInheritedTestUrl');
+  sql = postgres(env.TEST_DATABASE_URL, { max: 1, prepare: false, connect_timeout: 10 });
+  const evidence = await sql.begin('read only', async transaction => {
+    const [identity] = await transaction`select current_database() database_name`;
+    const tables = await transaction`select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public' order by tablename`;
+    if (identity.database_name !== databaseName) throw new Error('ConnectedDatabaseNameMismatch');
+    const counts = {};
+    for (const name of ['users','projects','documentation_bundles','user_api_keys','interview_sessions','interview_messages']) {
+      if (tables.some(t => t.tablename === name)) {
+        const [row] = await transaction`select count(*)::int count from public.${transaction(name)}`;
+        counts[name] = row.count;
+      }
+    }
+    return { connectedDatabase: identity.database_name, publicTableNames: tables.map(t => t.tablename), applicationRowCounts: counts };
+  });
+  result = { at: new Date().toISOString(), verified: true, testUrlPresent: true,
+    nameGuardSatisfied: true, applicationHostDifferent: testUrl.hostname !== appUrl.hostname,
+    applicationDatabaseNameDifferent: databaseName !== appDatabaseName, ...evidence, readOnly: true };
+} catch (error) {
+  result = { at: new Date().toISOString(), verified: false, readOnly: true,
+    ...configurationEvidence,
+    errorType: error.name, errorCode: error.code ?? null,
+    // Only explicit local validation labels; never print a driver error message.
+    validation: ['InvalidProtocol','GuardRejectedDatabaseName','ApplicationDatabaseTargetRejected',
+      'ConflictingInheritedTestUrl','ConnectedDatabaseNameMismatch'].includes(error.message) ? error.message : undefined };
+  process.exitCode = 1;
+} finally {
+  if (sql) await sql.end({ timeout: 5 });
+}
+if (output) fs.writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
+console.log(JSON.stringify(result));

SHA-256: 739745ad0324bea5f63a08ffea42fdc3641582069c0538bb2751cf2a23fe48dd

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/api/src/lib/crypto.unit.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { encryptKey, decryptKey, maskKey } from './crypto';
+
+describe('provider key encryption', () => {
+  it('roundtrips Unicode and uses a unique nonce per encryption', () => {
+    vi.stubEnv('ENCRYPTION_KEY', 'ab'.repeat(32));
+    const secret = 'fake-key-🔐-1234567890';
+    const first = encryptKey(secret), second = encryptKey(secret);
+    expect(first).not.toBe(second); expect(first).not.toContain(secret);
+    expect(decryptKey(first)).toBe(secret); expect(decryptKey(second)).toBe(secret);
+  });
+  it('rejects tampering and the wrong encryption key', () => {
+    vi.stubEnv('ENCRYPTION_KEY', 'ab'.repeat(32));
+    const cipher = encryptKey('fake-provider-key');
+    const bytes = Buffer.from(cipher, 'base64'); bytes[bytes.length - 1] ^= 1;
+    expect(() => decryptKey(bytes.toString('base64'))).toThrow();
+    vi.stubEnv('ENCRYPTION_KEY', 'cd'.repeat(32)); expect(() => decryptKey(cipher)).toThrow();
+  });
+  it.each(['', 'abc', 'z'.repeat(64)])('rejects invalid encryption configuration', value => {
+    vi.stubEnv('ENCRYPTION_KEY', value); expect(() => encryptKey('fake-key')).toThrow();
+  });
+  it.each(['short', '1234567890', 'sk-ant-test-12345678901234567890'])('never exposes the full secret in masks', key => {
+    expect(maskKey(key)).not.toContain(key);
+    // Even short accepted keys must retain hidden characters, not just insert dots.
+    expect(maskKey(key).replace(/•/g, '').length).toBeLessThan(key.length);
+  });
+});

+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

+
+const directories: string[] = [];
+afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllEnvs(); for (const dir of directories.splice(0)) fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true }); });
+function ledger() {
+  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'devdocs-budget-test-')); directories.push(dir);
+  const file = path.join(dir, 'spend.json'); vi.stubEnv('E2E_SPEND_LEDGER', file); return file;
+}
+async function harness(limit: number, max: number) {
+  let handler: any;
+  const page = { route: vi.fn(async (_pattern, fn) => { handler = fn; }) };
+  const info = { title: 'budget regression', attach: vi.fn(async () => {}) };
+  const snapshot = await guardLiveBudget(page as any, info as any, limit, max);
+  const route = { request: () => ({ postDataJSON: () => ({ provider: 'metamuse', projectId: 'test', domainId: 'planning' }), postData: () => '{}' }),
+    continue: vi.fn(async () => {}), abort: vi.fn(async () => {}) };
+  return { handler, route, snapshot };
+}
+describe('durable live provider spending guard', () => {
+  it('writes reservations before forwarding, and carries spend into later attempts', async () => {
+    const file = ledger(); const first = await harness(8.23, 30);
+    first.route.continue.mockImplementation(async () => { expect(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')).attempts).toHaveLength(1); });
+    await first.handler(first.route);
+    const second = await harness(8.23, 30); await second.handler(second.route);
+    expect(second.snapshot().newReservationUsd).toBeCloseTo(first.snapshot().newReservationUsd * 2);
+    expect(second.snapshot().cumulativeReservationUsd).toBeCloseTo(1.76834625 + second.snapshot().newReservationUsd);
+    expect(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')).attempts.every((a: any) => a.sdkAttemptsReserved === 3)).toBe(true);
+  });
+  it('blocks before forwarding when cumulative allowance would be exceeded', async () => {
+    const file = ledger(); const initial = await harness(0.2, 30); await initial.handler(initial.route);
+    const next = await harness(0.2, 30);
+    await expect(next.handler(next.route)).rejects.toThrow('budget reached');
+    expect(next.route.continue).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); expect(next.route.abort).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
+    expect(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')).attempts).toHaveLength(1);
+  });
+  it('retains the per-run request guard and refuses an unconfigured full interview', async () => {
+    ledger(); const run = await harness(8.23, 1); await run.handler(run.route);
+    await expect(run.handler(run.route)).rejects.toThrow('budget reached');
+    vi.stubEnv('E2E_SPEND_LEDGER', '');
+    await expect(harness(8.23, 30)).rejects.toThrow('require E2E_SPEND_LEDGER');
+  });
+});

apps/api/src/trpc/routers/keys.test.tsNew · +58 / −0

Add regression and behavior tests; 8 recorded executions in this report. See matching entries in the test ledger.

SHA-256: 54eae91ad5da65513eec2cee9a4cebbd50af310b188b147629118741079784c0

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/api/src/trpc/routers/keys.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
+import { appRouter } from '../router';
+import { createTestUser } from '../../test/helpers';
+import { db, userApiKeys } from '../../lib/db';
+import { decryptKey } from '../../lib/crypto';
+
+describe('key vault with real PostgreSQL and isolated provider verification', () => {
+  let owner: ReturnType<typeof appRouter.createCaller>;
+  let other: ReturnType<typeof appRouter.createCaller>;
+  let userId: string;
+  const key = 'sk-ant-fake-test-key-never-a-real-secret-1234567890';
+  beforeEach(async () => {
+    const user = await createTestUser(`keys-${crypto.randomUUID()}@example.test`);
+    const outsider = await createTestUser(`other-${crypto.randomUUID()}@example.test`);
+    userId = user.id;
+    owner = appRouter.createCaller({ userId: user.id, userEmail: user.email });
+    other = appRouter.createCaller({ userId: outsider.id, userEmail: outsider.email });
+    vi.stubEnv('ENCRYPTION_KEY', 'a'.repeat(64));
+    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(new Response('{}', { status: 200 })));
+  });
+  afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals(); vi.unstubAllEnvs(); });
+  it.each(['anthropic', 'openai', 'metamuse'] as const)('encrypts %s and returns only a masked key', async provider => {
+    const result = await owner.keys.upsert({ provider, key });
+    expect(result.maskedKey).not.toContain(key);
+    const [stored] = await db.select().from(userApiKeys).where(eq(userApiKeys.userId, userId));
+    expect(stored.keyHash).not.toContain(key);
+    expect(decryptKey(stored.keyHash)).toBe(key);
+    const listed = await owner.keys.list();
+    expect(listed).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(JSON.stringify(listed)).not.toMatch(/keyHash|ciphertext/);
+    expect(await other.keys.list()).toEqual([]);
+    await other.keys.delete({ provider });
+    expect(await owner.keys.list()).toHaveLength(1);
+    await owner.keys.delete({ provider });
+    expect(await owner.keys.list()).toEqual([]);
+  });
+  it('rotates a key without duplicate vault rows', async () => {
+    await owner.keys.upsert({ provider: 'anthropic', key });
+    const replacement = key + '-replacement';
+    await owner.keys.upsert({ provider: 'anthropic', key: replacement });
+    const rows = await db.select().from(userApiKeys).where(eq(userApiKeys.userId, userId));
+    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(decryptKey(rows[0].keyHash)).toBe(replacement);
+  });
+  it.each([401, 403, 500])('preserves the existing key on provider HTTP %s', async status => {
+    await owner.keys.upsert({ provider: 'anthropic', key });
+    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(new Response('{}', { status }));
+    await expect(owner.keys.upsert({ provider: 'anthropic', key: key + '-bad' })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'BAD_REQUEST' });
+    const [stored] = await db.select().from(userApiKeys).where(eq(userApiKeys.userId, userId));
+    expect(decryptKey(stored.keyHash)).toBe(key);
+  });
+  it('reports provider network failure without storing a key', async () => {
+    vi.mocked(fetch).mockRejectedValue(new Error('network unavailable'));
+    await expect(owner.keys.upsert({ provider: 'openai', key })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'BAD_REQUEST' });
+    expect(await owner.keys.list()).toEqual([]);
+  });
+});

diff --git a/apps/web/e2e/README.md b/apps/web/e2e/README.md
index 1654d01..491d970 100644
--- a/apps/web/e2e/README.md
+++ b/apps/web/e2e/README.md
@@ -1,14 +1,37 @@
 # E2E framework (`apps/web/e2e/`)
 
-Playwright + human-in-the-loop E2E for DevDocs AI. All specs import from
-`lib/fixtures.ts` — never from `@playwright/test` directly.
+Playwright E2E for DevDocs AI. Deterministic specs extend the shared monitoring
+framework through `lib/mock-fixtures.ts`; live specs use `lib/fixtures.ts`.
+
+## Test lanes
+
+| Command | Dependencies | Scope |
+|---|---|---|
+| `pnpm --filter @devdocs/web test:e2e` | Installed Chromium | Desktop and Pixel 7, stateful API simulator, development-only mock Clerk |
+| `pnpm --filter @devdocs/api test:unit` | None outside the workspace | Crypto, rate limits, AI HTTP/SSE boundaries and browser SSE parsing |
+| `pnpm --filter @devdocs/api test` | Disposable PostgreSQL database with `_test` in its name | Migrations, tRPC CRUD, ownership, documents, sessions, account data |
+| `pnpm --filter @devdocs/web test:e2e:hitl --headed` | Dedicated test account and authorized provider spend | Real Clerk, API, database and provider |
+
+The deterministic suite lives in `e2e/deterministic/`; the former
+`tests/e2e/` specs are superseded. It covers all six project types, active domain
+progression, reload, parsed ZIP contents, document edits, retry/failure paths,
+project actions, templates, key settings, privacy, search, deep links, mobile
+sheets, keyboard interaction, layout overflow, and Markdown sanitization.
+Screenshots are review artifacts, not pixel-comparison baselines.
+
+Mock traffic cannot prove database behavior, provider output quality, real
+authentication, or production capacity. The integration setup migrates and
+truncates its test database. Never provide a development or production database.
+Live tests can create projects and make billable AI requests; use a disposable
+account with a configured provider key. Saved sessions are validated against
+the dashboard; expired CI sessions fail with a refresh instruction.
 
 ## How this maps to the app
 
 | Framework piece | App structure it reflects |
 |---|---|
 | `lib/pages/DashboardPage.ts` | `/dashboard` — project grid + `CreateProjectModal` (project **type is captured once here** as a locked chip) |
-| `lib/pages/InterviewPage.ts` | `/project/[id]/interview` — hybrid single view with 3 regions: `DomainProgress` (left), `ChatPanel` (center, card pickers render **inline** via `showCards`), `PreviewPanel` (right, hidden until `isComplete`) |
+| `lib/pages/InterviewPage.ts` | `/project/[id]/interview` — progress, chat with inline card pickers, and per-domain document editing/export; mobile uses sheets |
 | `lib/pages/SettingsPage.ts` | `/settings` — sidebar sections; API keys go through typed tRPC mutations (never `localStorage`) |
 | `contracts/projects.list.schema.json` | tRPC `projects.list` (dashboard) |
 | `contracts/projects.get.schema.json` | tRPC `projects.get` (interview hydration) |
@@ -19,9 +42,49 @@ dashboard/settings/interview entry use `page.goto()`.
 
 ## Running
 
+For local live tests, start fresh API and web processes with `PLAYWRIGHT=0`.
+Archive `playwright-report/` and `test-results/` before running: both lanes use
+the same output paths. Set `SKIP_WEBSERVER=1` only after verifying those processes
+use real Clerk. Run `example.smoke.spec.ts --headed --workers=1` first; it waits
+for a successful authenticated `projects.list` response and completed contract
+validation. The live lane contains authentication setup, dashboard smoke,
+partial/full interviews, document editing/export and desktop/mobile library
+checks; it does not run the deterministic cases against real services. Agree on a
+provider spending limit before running `interview.e2e.spec.ts`.
+
+For the currently budgeted Meta Muse flow, set `E2E_PROVIDER=metamuse` and
+`E2E_PROVIDER_SPEND_USD` to the remaining authorized USD amount. The test selects
+the existing provider through Settings, permits at most five real generation
+requests, reserves input/output cost including SDK retries, waits for planning
+and architecture completion, and reloads to verify saved progress. Subtract
+reservations recorded by previous attempts when retrying. The reservation is a
+conservative bound, not a provider invoice. Other providers currently skip this
+budgeted flow until their pricing calculation is configured. No keys are entered
+or reverified by this test.
+
+Full SaaS validation uses `full-live.e2e.spec.ts` with a deliberate 30-request
+per-attempt guard. Set `PLAYWRIGHT=0`, `ENABLE_AI_TRIAGE=false`,

apps/web/e2e/lib/live-budget.tsNew · +49 / −0

Durably reserve Meta Muse cost before forwarding each request; retain cumulative spend across attempts and bound SDK retries.

SHA-256: 202c73f97861d0d02ce109a93edfd538718e0c990b51e9618cf40fb5c2f53254

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/web/e2e/lib/live-budget.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import type { Page, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';
+import { META_MUSE_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS } from '@devdocs/shared';
+
+/** Persist reservations BEFORE forwarding traffic, including all three SDK attempts. */
+export async function guardLiveBudget(page: Page, info: TestInfo, limitUsd: number, maxRequests = 5) {
+  const ledgerPath = process.env.E2E_SPEND_LEDGER;
+  if (maxRequests > 5 && !ledgerPath) throw new Error('Full interviews require E2E_SPEND_LEDGER');
+  const ledger = ledgerPath && fs.existsSync(ledgerPath)
+    ? JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(ledgerPath, 'utf8'))
+    : { previousReservationUsd: 1.76834625, allowanceUsd: limitUsd, attempts: [] };
+  if (ledger.allowanceUsd !== limitUsd || !(limitUsd > 0 && limitUsd <= 8.23)) {
+    throw new Error('Live allowance must match the cumulative ledger and remain within $8.23');
+  }
+  let requests = 0;
+  const snapshot = () => {
+    const newReservationUsd = ledger.attempts.reduce((sum: number, attempt: { reservationUsd: number }) => sum + attempt.reservationUsd, 0);
+    return { requests, maxRequests, newReservationUsd, previousReservationUsd: ledger.previousReservationUsd,
+      cumulativeReservationUsd: ledger.previousReservationUsd + newReservationUsd,
+      remainingAllowanceUsd: limitUsd - newReservationUsd, exactBilling: 'unverified' };
+  };
+  await page.route('**/ai/stream', async route => {
+    const request = route.request();
+    const body = request.postDataJSON();
+    if (body.provider !== 'metamuse') {
+      await route.abort('blockedbyclient');
+      throw new Error('The live budget guard supports only Meta Muse');
+    }
+    // Payload bytes bound variable prompt/history tokens; 20k covers fixed system
+    // instructions and framing. Reserve full reasoning + visible output budget.
+    const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(request.postData() ?? '', 'utf8');
+    const reservationUsd = 3 * ((bytes + 20_000) * 1.25 / 1_000_000 + META_MUSE_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS * 4.25 / 1_000_000);
+    if (requests >= maxRequests || snapshot().newReservationUsd + reservationUsd > limitUsd) {
+      await route.abort('blockedbyclient');
+      throw new Error('Cumulative live interview generation budget reached');
+    }
+    requests++;
+    ledger.attempts.push({ at: new Date().toISOString(), test: info.title, projectId: body.projectId,
+      domainId: body.domainId, persistDocument: body.persistDocument, payloadBytes: bytes, sdkAttemptsReserved: 3, reservationUsd });
+    if (ledgerPath) {
+      fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(ledgerPath), { recursive: true });
+      fs.writeFileSync(ledgerPath, JSON.stringify(ledger, null, 2));
+    }
+    await info.attach(`provider-budget-${requests}`, { body: JSON.stringify(snapshot()), contentType: 'application/json' });
+    await route.continue();
+  });
+  return snapshot;
+}

Capture read-only configured PostgreSQL evidence for explicitly identified live test projects.

SHA-256: 2236ee57321d5633bda674be24a20e7f7ae63c7389ed1fc7e3480bb8bfc3c07a

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/web/e2e/lib/live-evidence.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import type { TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';
+
+export interface LiveEvidence {
+  project: { id: string; name: string; type: string; status: string; interview_data: {
+    completedDomains: string[]; lockedChoices: Record<string, Record<string, string>>;
+    conversationHistory: { role: string; content: string; domainId?: string; showCards?: string }[];
+  } };
+  documents: { domain_id: string; content: string }[];
+  sessions: { id: string; total_domains_completed: number; is_complete: boolean; primary_provider: string | null }[];
+  messageCounts: unknown[];
+}
+
+export function readLiveEvidence(projectId: string): LiveEvidence {
+  return JSON.parse(execFileSync(process.execPath, [path.resolve('../api/scripts/live-project-evidence.mjs'), projectId],
+    { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 30_000, windowsHide: true }));
+}
+
+export async function captureLiveEvidence(projectId: string, name: string, info: TestInfo) {
+  const evidence = readLiveEvidence(projectId);
+  const file = info.outputPath(`${name}.json`);
+  fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(evidence, null, 2));
+  await info.attach(name, { path: file, contentType: 'application/json' });
+  return evidence;
+}

+import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';
+import type { DomainId, ProjectType } from '@devdocs/shared';
+import { getActiveDomains } from '../../../lib/interview/domains';
+
+export const PROJECT_ID = '00000000-0000-4000-a000-000000000001';
+export const context = { projectType: 'saas' as ProjectType, teamSize: 'small', timeline: '1_3_months', budget: 'bootstrapped', experienceLevel: 'intermediate' };
+export function project(type: ProjectType = 'saas', completed = 0) {
+  const domains = getActiveDomains(type);
+  return {
+    id: PROJECT_ID, name: 'Team Planner', type, status: completed === domains.length ? 'complete' : 'in_progress',
+    description: 'Planning workspace', domainsCompleted: completed, updatedAt: 'Just now',
+    interviewData: {
+      lockedContext: { ...context, projectType: type }, lockedChoices: {},
+      completedDomains: domains.slice(0, completed).map(d => d.id),
+      conversationHistory: domains.slice(0, completed).map(d => ({ role: 'assistant', content: `## ${d.label}\n\nSaved ${d.id} decisions.`, domainId: d.id })),
+      elaboration: 'A planning workspace for remote teams',
+    },
+    documents: domains.slice(0, completed).map(d => ({ id: `${PROJECT_ID}-${d.id}`, projectId: PROJECT_ID, domainId: d.id, content: `## ${d.label}\n\nSaved ${d.id} decisions.`, createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' })),
+  };
+}
+type MockProject = Omit<ReturnType<typeof project>, 'interviewData'> & { interviewData: any };
+type Failure = { message: string; code?: string; remaining?: number };
+export type StreamMode = 'success' | 'auth' | 'rate_limit' | 'persistence' | 'empty' | 'eof' | 'malformed' | 'network' | 'pending';
+
+/** A per-test stateful API simulator. Unknown procedures fail instead of
+ * silently returning a successful shape. This is not a substitute for API tests. */
+export class MockApplication {
+  projects: MockProject[] = [project()];
+  keys = [{ provider: 'anthropic', maskedKey: 'sk-ant-••••1234', createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' }];
+  bedrock = false;
+  failures: Record<string, Failure> = {};
+  streamMode: StreamMode = 'success';
+  calls: { procedure: string; input: any }[] = [];
+  streams: any[] = [];
+  unexpected: string[] = [];
+  private sequence = 1;
+  constructor(private page: Page) {}
+
+  fail(procedure: string, message = 'Service temporarily unavailable', remaining = Infinity, code = 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR') {
+    this.failures[procedure] = { message, remaining, code };
+  }
+  async install() {
+    await this.page.route('**/trpc/**', async route => {
+      const request = route.request();
+      if (request.method() === 'OPTIONS') { await route.fulfill({ status: 204, headers: { 'access-control-allow-origin': '*', 'access-control-allow-headers': '*' } }); return; }
+      const url = new URL(request.url());
+      const procedures = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.split('/trpc/')[1]).split(',');
+      const batch = url.searchParams.get('batch') === '1';
+      const input = request.method() === 'GET' ? JSON.parse(url.searchParams.get('input') ?? '{}') : request.postDataJSON();
+      const results = procedures.map((procedure, i) => {
+        const data = batch ? input?.[String(i)] : input;
+        this.calls.push({ procedure, input: data });
+        const failure = this.failures[procedure];
+        if (failure && (failure.remaining ?? 0) > 0) {
+          failure.remaining!--;
+          return { error: { message: failure.message, code: -32603, data: { code: failure.code, httpStatus: failure.code === 'NOT_FOUND' ? 404 : 500, path: procedure } } };
+        }
+        try { return { result: { data: this.respond(procedure, data) } }; }
+        catch (error) { return { error: { message: String(error), code: -32603, data: { code: 'NOT_FOUND', httpStatus: 404, path: procedure } } }; }
+      });
+      await route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(batch ? results : results[0]) });
+    });
+    await this.page.route('**/ai/bedrock-status', route => route.fulfill({ json: { configured: this.bedrock, region: this.bedrock ? 'us-east-1' : null, model: this.bedrock ? 'test-model' : null } }));
+    await this.page.route('**/ai/stream', async route => {
+      const input = route.request().postDataJSON();
+      this.streams.push(input);
+      if (this.streamMode === 'pending') return;
+      if (this.streamMode === 'network') { await route.abort('failed'); return; }
+      if (this.streamMode === 'auth' || this.streamMode === 'rate_limit') {
+        await route.fulfill({ status: this.streamMode === 'auth' ? 401 : 429, json: { message: this.streamMode === 'auth' ? 'Provider key rejected' : 'Rate limit reached. Try again shortly.' } }); return;
+      }
+      let body: string;
+      const text = `## ${input.domainId}\n\nGenerated ${input.domainId} decisions for the project.`;
+      if (this.streamMode === 'persistence') body = `data: ${JSON.stringify({ type: 'error', errorType: 'persistence', message: 'The response could not be saved. Please retry.' })}\n\n`;
+      else if (this.streamMode === 'malformed') body = 'data: invalid-json\n\n';
+      else if (this.streamMode === 'eof') body = `data: ${JSON.stringify({ type: 'token', text: 'Incomplete response' })}\n\n`;
+      else {
+        const content = this.streamMode === 'empty' ? '' : text;
+        if (input.persistDocument && content) this.saveDocument(input.projectId, input.domainId, content);
+        body = `data: ${JSON.stringify({ type: 'token', text: content.slice(0, 8) })}\n\ndata: ${JSON.stringify({ type: 'token', text: content.slice(8) })}\n\ndata: ${JSON.stringify({ type: 'done', text: content })}\n\n`;
+      }
+      await route.fulfill({ contentType: 'text/event-stream', body });
+    });
+  }
+  private saveDocument(projectId: string, domainId: DomainId, content: string) {
+    const p = this.projects.find(p => p.id === projectId)!;
+    const previous = p.documents.find(d => d.domainId === domainId);
+    if (previous) previous.content = content;
+    else p.documents.push({ id: `${projectId}-${domainId}`, projectId, domainId, content, createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' });
+    return p.documents.find(d => d.domainId === domainId);
+  }
+  private respond(name: string, input: any): unknown {
+    switch (name) {
+      case 'projects.list': return this.projects;
+      case 'projects.get': { const p = this.projects.find(p => p.id === input.id); if (!p) throw new Error('Project not found'); return p; }
+      case 'projects.create': {
+        const p = { ...project(input.type), id: `00000000-0000-4000-a000-${String(++this.sequence).padStart(12, '0')}`, name: input.name, interviewData: null, documents: [] };
+        this.projects.push(p); return p;
+      }
+      case 'projects.update': {
+        const p = this.projects.find(p => p.id === input.id)!;
+        Object.assign(p, input.data);
+        p.domainsCompleted = p.interviewData?.completedDomains?.length ?? 0;
+        return p;
+      }
+      case 'projects.delete': this.projects = this.projects.filter(p => p.id !== input.id); return { success: true };
+      case 'documents.list': return this.projects.flatMap(p => p.documents.map(d => ({ ...d, projectName: p.name, projectType: p.type })));
+      case 'documents.listByProject': return this.projects.find(p => p.id === input.projectId)?.documents ?? [];
+      case 'documents.update': return this.saveDocument(input.projectId, input.domainId, input.content);
+      case 'keys.list': return this.keys;
+      case 'keys.upsert': {
+        const key = { provider: input.provider, maskedKey: `${input.provider}-••••1234`, createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' };
+        this.keys = [...this.keys.filter(k => k.provider !== input.provider), key]; return key;
+      }
+      case 'keys.delete': this.keys = this.keys.filter(k => k.provider !== input.provider); return { success: true };
+      case 'sessions.create': return { id: '00000000-0000-4000-a000-000000000099' };
+      case 'sessions.logMessage': case 'sessions.update': return { success: true };
+      case 'account.exportData': return { user: { email: 'tester@example.test' }, projects: this.projects, apiKeys: this.keys };
+      case 'account.deleteData': this.projects = []; this.keys = []; return { success: true };
+      default: this.unexpected.push(name); throw new Error(`Unmocked procedure: ${name}`);
+    }
+  }
+}

Classify only same-origin GET Server Component requests cancelled with ERR_ABORTED; retain cancellation evidence and all API failures.

SHA-256: 0cb0c8aa72830396b1cf0738898c33fb425f44d2b202ee6bdcb82343cdd12ad4

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/web/e2e/lib/monitoring/cancellation.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+/** Next cancels superseded same-origin Server Component navigation fetches. */
+export function expectedNavigationCancellation(method: string, url: string, pageUrl: string, rsc: string | undefined, failure: string): boolean {
+  if (method !== 'GET' || rsc !== '1' || failure !== 'net::ERR_ABORTED') return false;
+  try {
+    const target = new URL(url);
+    return target.origin === new URL(pageUrl).origin && target.searchParams.has('_rsc');
+  } catch { return false; }
+}

apps/web/e2e/lib/monitoring/redact.tsNew · +23 / −0

Redact session, handshake, bearer and JWT values in readable browser monitoring artifacts.

SHA-256: 88ae2935a7106d26bdfb7defc6907aaf299140cd510063eb7c71cb0536c1fead

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/web/e2e/lib/monitoring/redact.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+/** Keep authentication material out of readable monitoring artifacts. */
+export function redactText(text: string): string {
+  return text
+    .replace(/\bBearer\s+[^\s"'<>]+/gi, 'Bearer [redacted]')
+    .replace(/\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\b/g, '[redacted]')
+    .replace(/([?&](?:__[^=&\s]*|[^=&\s]*(?:token|secret|password|api[_-]?key)|code|state)=)[^&\s"'<>]+/gi, '$1[redacted]');
+}
+
+export function redactUrl(value: string, depth = 0): string {
+  try {
+    const url = new URL(value);
+    url.username = '';
+    url.password = '';
+    for (const [key, field] of [...url.searchParams]) {
+      if (/^__|token|secret|password|api[_-]?key|^(code|state)$/i.test(key)) {
+        url.searchParams.set(key, '[redacted]');
+      } else if (depth < 3 && /^https?:\/\//i.test(field)) {
+        url.searchParams.set(key, redactUrl(field, depth + 1));
+      }
+    }
+    return redactText(url.toString());
+  } catch { return redactText(value); }
+}

+import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
+import { BasePage } from './BasePage';
+import { pauseForHuman } from '../hitl/pauseForHuman';
+
+export class AuthenticationPage extends BasePage {
+  async dashboard() {
+    await this.goto('/dashboard');
+    await expect(this.page.getByRole('button', { name: /New project/i }).first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 60_000 });
+    await expect.poll(async () => this.page.evaluate(() => !!(window as any).Clerk?.session)).toBe(true);
+  }
+  async humanAuth(label: string, signup = false) {
+    await this.goto(signup ? '/sign-up' : '/sign-in');
+    if (!signup) {
+      await expect.poll(() => this.page.evaluate(() => !!(window as any).Clerk?.loaded), { timeout: 60_000 }).toBe(true);
+      if (await this.page.evaluate(() => !!(window as any).Clerk?.user && !!(window as any).Clerk?.session)) {
+        await this.dashboard();
+        return;
+      }
+    }
+    await expect(this.page.locator(signup ? '.cl-signUp-root' : '.cl-signIn-root')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 60_000 });
+    await pauseForHuman({ page: this.page, testInfo: this.testInfo, timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000,
+      reason: signup ? `Create NEW disposable auth-test account ${label}. ${label === 'B' ? 'This account is dedicated to deletion in this run.' : 'Do not use an existing account.'}` : `Sign in again to ${label}. Complete CAPTCHA/MFA in this browser.`,
+      resumeWhen: async () => this.page.evaluate(() => !!(window as any).Clerk?.user && !!(window as any).Clerk?.session) });
+    await this.dashboard();
+  }
+  async signOut() {
+    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Account menu', exact: true }).click();
+    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign out', exact: true }).click();
+    await expect.poll(() => this.page.evaluate(() => !(window as any).Clerk?.session), { timeout: 60_000 }).toBe(true);
+  }
+  async expectPrivateAbsent(names: string[]) {
+    for (const name of names) await expect(this.page.getByText(name, { exact: true })).toHaveCount(0, { timeout: 30_000 });
+  }
+  async signInRecoverable() {
+    await this.goto('/sign-in');
+    await expect(this.page.locator('.cl-signIn-root')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 60_000 });
+  }
+  async deleteLocalData() {
+    await this.goto('/settings?section=privacy');
+    const button = this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete data & continue', exact: true });
+    await expect(button).toBeDisabled();
+    await this.page.getByPlaceholder('DELETE', { exact: true }).fill('DELETE');
+    await expect(button).toBeEnabled();
+    const response = this.page.waitForResponse(r => new URL(r.url()).pathname.includes('account.deleteData'));
+    await button.click();
+    expect((await response).status()).toBe(200);
+    await expect(this.page.locator('.cl-userProfile-root')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 60_000 });
+  }
+  async ownershipUi(projectId: string, forbiddenName: string, forbiddenBody: string) {
+    await this.dashboard();
+    await this.expectPrivateAbsent([forbiddenName]);
+    await this.goto('/docs');
+    await this.expectPrivateAbsent([forbiddenName, forbiddenBody]);
+    await this.goto(`/project/${projectId}/interview`);
+    await expect(this.page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('Unable to load this project', { timeout: 60_000 });
+    await this.expectPrivateAbsent([forbiddenName, forbiddenBody]);
+    await expect(this.page.getByRole('button', { name: /Download|Save changes|Rename|Delete project/ })).toHaveCount(0);
+  }
+}

apps/web/e2e/lib/pages/WorkspacePage.tsNew · +78 / −0

Add semantic workspace helpers, enabled-choice selection and dialog-scoped downloads.

SHA-256: ec891b10e9cfda9049428df10a477841eb5f25758bc5441c2c450a24b420f409

--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/web/e2e/lib/pages/WorkspacePage.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+import { expect, type Download } from '@playwright/test';
+import { BasePage } from './BasePage';
+
+/** Shared semantic UI surface for the deterministic suite. */
+export class WorkspacePage extends BasePage {
+  async goto(path: string) {
+    await super.goto(path);
+    await this.page.locator('html[data-e2e-hydrated="true"]').waitFor({ state: 'attached' });
+  }
+  button(name: string | RegExp) { return this.page.getByRole('button', { name }).filter({ visible: true }); }
+  text(text: string | RegExp) { return this.page.getByText(text).filter({ visible: true }); }
+  heading(name: string | RegExp) { return this.page.getByRole('heading', { name }).filter({ visible: true }); }
+  input(placeholder: string | RegExp) { return this.page.getByPlaceholder(placeholder).filter({ visible: true }); }
+  get alert() { return this.page.getByRole('alert').filter({ visible: true }); }
+  get radios() { return this.page.getByRole('radio', { disabled: false }).filter({ visible: true }); }
+  get editor() { return this.page.getByRole('textbox').filter({ visible: true }); }
+  get dialogs() { return this.page.getByRole('dialog'); }
+  field(name: string) { return this.page.getByRole('textbox', { name, exact: true }).filter({ visible: true }); }
+  async click(name: string | RegExp) { await this.button(name).first().click(); }
+  async fill(placeholder: string | RegExp, value: string) { await this.input(placeholder).fill(value); }
+  async reload() { await this.page.reload(); }
+  async keyboard(key: string) { await this.page.keyboard.press(key); }
+  async openProject(id: string) { await this.goto(`/project/${id}/interview`); }
+  async waitForInterviewRoute() {
+    await this.page.waitForURL(/\/project\/.+\/interview/, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: 60_000 });
+  }
+  async waitForDiscovery() {
+    // Creation finishes before Next navigation and project hydration. Wait for
+    // both boundaries before asserting discovery, as the onboarding lane does.
+    await this.waitForInterviewRoute();
+    await expect(this.heading('A few quick questions')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 45_000 });
+  }
+  async waitForInterview() {
+    await this.waitForInterviewRoute();
+    await expect(this.input('Type your answer...')).toBeEnabled({ timeout: 45_000 });
+    await expect(this.button('Try again')).toHaveCount(0);
+  }
+  async waitForMockSignIn() {
+    await this.page.waitForURL(/\/sign-in(?:[/?]|$)/, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: 60_000 });
+    await expect(this.text('Mock sign-in boundary')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 45_000 });
+  }
+  async discover() {
+    for (const name of ['2-3 people', '1-3 months', 'Bootstrapped', 'Intermediate']) await this.click(name);
+    await this.click(/Start planning/);
+  }
+  async answer(text: string) {
+    await this.fill(/Type your answer|Ask a question/, text);
+    await this.click('Send');
+  }
+  async chooseFirstCard() { await this.radios.first().click(); }
+  async expectViewportFits() {
+    const size = await this.page.evaluate(() => ({ width: document.documentElement.clientWidth, scroll: document.documentElement.scrollWidth }));
+    expect(size.scroll, 'No horizontal document overflow').toBeLessThanOrEqual(size.width + 1);
+  }
+  async expectControlInViewport(name: string | RegExp) {
+    const box = await this.button(name).first().boundingBox();
+    expect(box).not.toBeNull();
+    const viewport = this.page.viewportSize()!;
+    expect(box!.x).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
+    expect(box!.x + box!.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(viewport.width + 1);
+  }
+  async download(name: string | RegExp): Promise<Download> {
+    const dialog = this.dialogs.filter({ visible: true });
+    const control = await dialog.count() ? dialog.getByRole('button', { name }).first() : this.button(name).first();
+    const [download] = await Promise.all([this.page.waitForEvent('download'), control.click()]);
+    return download;
+  }
+  async storedPreferences() { return this.page.evaluate(() => ({ ...localStorage })); }
+  async setPreference(key: string, value: string) { await this.page.addInitScript(({ key, value }) => localStorage.setItem(key, value), { key, value }); }
+  async expectNoExecutableMarkdown() {
+    expect(await this.page.evaluate(() => (window as any).__xss)).toBeUndefined();
+    await expect(this.page.locator('a[href^="javascript:"], img[onerror], script[data-xss]')).toHaveCount(0);
+  }
+  async confirmPrompt(value: string) { this.page.once('dialog', dialog => dialog.accept(value)); }
+  async expectFocusInsideDialog() {
+    expect(await this.page.evaluate(() => !!document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]'))).toBe(true);
+  }
+}
